To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the disintermediating actions of hotels can be destructive to agents and the hotel industry, and that the key to a win-win situation is the quality of relationships between agents and hotels.

the hotel's online channel will not completely replace the traditional distribution channel, and that the online channel will not necessarily be a destructive act to agents, but will be a complementary channel that can improve the quality of the relationship between hotels and travel agents.

the trend of dis- intermediation is threatening travel agents, that travel agents have to take actions to fight against the destructive acts of hotels, and that hotels can improve their relationship with agents by offering them better commission rates and by providing them with better service.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the survival of travel agents in a world of disintermediated hotel distribution.
the survival of the travel agent in the hotel industry in the face of the disintermediating trend.
the impact of the online channel on the relationship between hotels and their travel agents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the disintermediated hotel should take the following measures in order to improve their relationship with the agent and to reduce the negative impact on them: (1) the hotel should provide the agent with a good commission structure; (2) the hotel should give the agent a better rate than the public rate; (3) the hotel should allow the agent to have a better rate than that of the public rate; and (4) the hotel should offer the agent a better service than that of the hotel
disintermediation can be a win-win situation for hotels and travel agents if they work together and understand each other's needs.
hotels should not take distribution back into own hands.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
disintermediation in the hotel industry is a two-way street: hotels can use their online channel to bypass travel agents and agents can use their own online channel to bypass hotels.
the disintermediating trend in the hospitality industry is inevitable and that travel agents need to change their traditional way of doing business.
hotels should take into consideration the agents' interests in their online distribution strategies.
The main takeaway from our work is that

disintermediation can only be stopped if the relationship between hotels and agents is strengthened, which is possible only when the hotel's online channel is designed and operated with the agent's needs and interests in mind.
hotels should consider the impact of their actions on their agents when they decide whether to disintermediate them.
disintermediation in the travel agent market is not a one-way process.
